whys.why: Why does package-manifest-port.ts import createRequire from node:module?
whys.because: It finds where a package's manifest is installed, starting the search at whichever folder the caller names.

whys.why: Why does the caller name the folder the manifest search starts at?
whys.because: The speed baseline compares two Hone builds, so it checks that every sample copy loads its own side's build.

whys.why: Why might a sample copy load a build that is not its own side's?
whys.because: Nothing is installed in a sample copy: it is a git worktree placed inside its side's install folder, so its packages are found in a folder above it.

whys.why: Why does being placed below another folder settle which packages a copy finds?
whys.because: Node looks in the node_modules folder of the starting folder, then of each parent folder, until it finds the package.

whys.why: Why ask Node for that lookup rather than walk the parent folders ourselves?
whys.because: Node owns that lookup, and module.createRequire gives a require function for a file path the caller chooses.

whyChain.rootCause: Node owns the package lookup and offers it from a chosen path through module.createRequire.
whyChain.rootEvidence: Read 25 Nov 2026: src/infrastructure/node/modules/package-manifest-port.ts:15 calls createRequire(...).resolve, its only use of node:module.
whyChain.readback: Node owns the package lookup and offers it through createRequire; therefore the folders above a sample copy settle which packages it finds; therefore the baseline checks that each copy finds its own side's build; therefore the caller names the folder to search from; therefore package-manifest-port.ts imports createRequire from node:module.
